title: Binary Search Tree Iterator

content.problemStatement:
Binary trees in these problems are encoded as a flat array named `tree` using complete-binary-tree (heap) indexing:

- the root sits at index 0
- a node at index `i` has its left child at index `2*i+1` and right child at index `2*i+2`
- a child index only counts as real if it's within the array bounds **and** its value isn't the sentinel `-101`, which means "no node there"

The given tree is always a valid binary search tree.

**Design an iterator that walks the tree's nodes in ascending (inorder) order, supporting `next` (returns the value of the next smallest node not yet returned, and advances past it) and `hasNext` (reports whether any node remains to be returned).**

Since this problem asks for a single pure function rather than a stateful object, you're given the tree plus a space-delimited string of operations (each token either "next" or "hasNext"). Simulate a freshly constructed iterator running through each operation in order, and return a list of results: the returned value for each "next", and 1 or 0 for each "hasNext".
constraints: the given tree always satisfies the binary search tree property
every "next" token in ops is only ever called when a preceding hasNext (implicit or checked) would have returned true
content.inputFormat: Single line: JSON array of all arguments, e.g. [arg1, arg2, ...]

sampleTestCases.input: tree = [7, 3, 15, -101, -101, 9, 20], ops = "next next hasNext next hasNext"
sampleTestCases.explanation: inorder order is 3, 7, 9, 15, 20; the first two next calls return 3 and 7, hasNext is true since 9, 15, 20 remain, next returns 9, and hasNext is still true since 15 and 20 remain
a single-node tree: hasNext is true before any calls, next returns the only value 1, and hasNext is false afterward since nothing remains
inorder order is 1, 2, 3; after three next calls every node has been returned, so the final hasNext is false

hints: Identify the search space and verify that the condition is monotonic (true...true...false...false).
Be mindful of integer overflow when computing mid: use mid = left + (right - left) // 2.
Ensure the termination condition (left <= right vs left < right) correctly handles boundary elements.
